title: Constraints Determine Output
equation: Max Output = Capacity of the Weakest Constraint
hook: Great marketing doesn't matter if fulfillment can't keep up. The slowest part of the business sets the pace.
statement: The weakest link sets the limit for the whole system.
explainer: Improving the parts that are already good feels productive, but it doesn't raise output. Only widening the bottleneck does. Everything else is just waiting in line.
sop: Map your process end to end.
Score each stage's capacity 1 to 10 and find the lowest.
Ignore every other stage until that one improves.
Add capacity, cut a step, or delegate right at that point.
Re-map afterward, because the bottleneck usually moves.
equation_example: Marketing 9, Sales 8, Fulfillment 3, Support 7. Max Output is the lowest one, 3. Not the average. Higher means even your weakest part is strong. Lower means one stage is capping everything else.
question: Name the one constraint you've been working around instead of fixing.
closing_statement: Fix the weakest link, not the strongest one.
caption:
Principle Nº 105: Constraints Determine Output

Great marketing doesn't matter if fulfillment can't keep up. The slowest part of the business sets the pace.

The weakest link sets the limit for the whole system.

Your turn: Name the one constraint you've been working around instead of fixing.
